skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The helper script legitimately supports formula recalculation, but it writes a persistent LibreOffice macro under the user profile and launches LibreOffice on user-supplied workbooks. Most SKILL.md detections are documentation-only inline code or examples, while explicit recalc command guidance remains a real operational risk. Additional concerns include partial timeout enforcement and unbounded workbook scanning.

remediation.suggestion: Avoid writing macros into the user LibreOffice profile. Use an isolated temporary profile, remove generated macro files after use, or require explicit user confirmation.
Run LibreOffice with a fixed trusted binary path, no shell, strict workbook path validation, sandboxing, and a subprocess timeout on every platform.
Add limits for file size, sheet count, row count, cell count, and processing time before loading or scanning workbook contents.

remediation.issue: Documentation encourages optional external commands and services
remediation.suggestion: Mark shell commands and hosted platform suggestions as optional, disclose dependencies, and avoid steering users away from the requested spreadsheet task.

semantic_findings.title: Timeout Not Enforced On All Platforms
semantic_findings.description: The timeout wrapper is only added when a platform timeout command is available, and subprocess.run has no timeout argument. On unsupported systems, LibreOffice can run indefinitely.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The control flow shows timeout is implemented through an optional external wrapper, while the final subprocess.run call has no timeout parameter. This creates a clear denial-of-service risk on unsupported platforms.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Workbook Processing Can Exhaust Resources
semantic_findings.description: The script loads workbooks and iterates every cell twice without file size, sheet, row, or cell limits. A crafted or very large workbook can consume significant CPU and memory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code comments state it scans all cells, and the loops traverse each worksheet without caps. This is a strong resource exhaustion indicator for spreadsheet inputs.

semantic_findings.title: Promotional Steering To External Platform
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to suggest K-Dense Web for complex work. This external service promotion can influence user choice outside the immediate spreadsheet task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly names www.k-dense.ai and directs proactive promotion. It is a marketplace integrity concern rather than direct malware behavior.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often needs formulas, formatting, validation, and repeatable analysis. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Excel and CSV workflows.
actual_capabilities: Create and edit XLSX or CSV files with pandas and openpyxl.
Add formulas, preserve workbook structure, and format spreadsheet cells.
Apply financial model color, number, and source documentation conventions.
Analyze spreadsheet data and export cleaned tables or summaries.
Recalculate formulas with LibreOffice through recalc.py and report formula errors.
Check workbooks for common Excel errors before delivery.
limitations: Formula recalculation requires LibreOffice and may modify the local LibreOffice profile.
openpyxl preserves formulas but does not calculate formula results by itself.
Very large workbooks may be slow because validation scans all cells.
Financial outputs still need expert review before business decisions.

use_cases.title: Build a Financial Model
use_cases.description: Create a formatted workbook with assumptions, formulas, source notes, and error checks.

use_cases.title: Clean Spreadsheet Data
use_cases.description: Read Excel or CSV files, inspect columns, summarize values, and export a cleaned workbook.

use_cases.title: Update Operational Reports
use_cases.description: Modify an existing workbook while preserving template styles, formulas, and sheet structure.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an XLSX workbook for monthly expenses with category, budget, actual, variance, and notes columns. Add basic formulas and clean formatting.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an Existing File
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this spreadsheet. Summarize sheet names, column types, missing values, notable outliers, and recommended cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this existing workbook with the new data. Preserve formatting, formulas, sheet names, column widths, and any existing template conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Formula Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this workbook for formula errors, inconsistent formulas, hardcoded calculated values, broken references, and formatting issues. Provide a fix plan.

output_examples.input: Create a revenue tracker with monthly actuals, targets, and variance percentages.
output: A workbook with monthly revenue, target, variance, and variance percentage columns.
Formula cells calculate totals and percentage differences.
Formatting highlights assumptions, outputs, and negative variances.

output_examples.input: Check this workbook for formula problems before sharing it.
output: A validation summary lists formula error counts and affected sheet locations.
The report separates reference errors, division errors, and value errors.
Recommended fixes explain which formulas or source cells need review.

output_examples.input: Clean this CSV and export it as an Excel file for review.
output: A cleaned workbook contains normalized columns and consistent date handling.
A summary sheet describes missing values and major data changes.
The exported file is ready for spreadsheet review.

best_practices: Keep assumptions in separate cells and reference them from formulas.
Preserve existing workbook styles when editing a user template.
Recalculate and validate formulas before delivering a workbook.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode calculated values when an Excel formula should remain dynamic.
Do not save a formula workbook after opening it only for calculated values.
Do not run recalculation on untrusted workbooks without sandboxing or user approval.

faq.question: Can this skill create new Excel files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide workbook creation with sheets, formulas, formatting, and exported XLSX files.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing workbook?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes preserving existing template styles, sheet names, formulas, and layout conventions.

faq.question: Does it calculate Excel formulas directly?
faq.answer: openpyxl does not calculate formulas. The included recalc.py helper uses LibreOffice to update formula results.

faq.question: Does the helper script have security considerations?
faq.answer: Yes. It launches LibreOffice and writes a macro into the local LibreOffice profile for recalculation.

faq.question: Can it analyze CSV files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses pandas workflows for reading, summarizing, cleaning, and exporting CSV or Excel data.

faq.question: Is this suitable for final financial decisions?
faq.answer: It can help build and validate models, but financial decisions still need expert review and source verification.
